entities.summary:
Quintus Hortensius was a Roman politician who was elected consul for 108 BC, but was prosecuted before he could take office.


Hortensius was a key figure in the late Roman Republic, where he played a significant role in the struggle for power and influence. He was a member of the Optimates, a conservative faction that sought to limit the power of the popular assemblies.


His prosecution was a major event in the history of the Roman Republic, as it marked a turning point in the struggle between the Optimates and the Populares, two of the main factions of the time. The outcome of the case had significant consequences for the future of the Republic, as it led to the rise of the Populares and the eventual transformation of the Roman government.


The legacy of Hortensius can be seen in the many historians and scholars who have studied his case, as it provides a unique window into the politics and intrigue of the late Roman Republic.


'For the sake of the Republic, I would sacrifice my own life.' - Quintus Hortensius
